tagline.text: The first SM mall, opened in 1985, and a giant complex at the north end of Quezon City

location.label: Location

children.text: SM North EDSA is the first SM Supermall, opened in 1985, a large complex at the north end of EDSA in Quezon City. Its linked shopping buildings include the Sky Garden, cinemas and food courts, and it connects directly to MRT-3 North Avenue station.

SM North EDSA is a shopping mall built by SM Prime Holdings, the Philippines' largest retail group, at the corner where the EDSA highway meets North Avenue in northern Quezon City. According to Wikipedia, it opened in
November 1985
as
the first SM Supermall

on about 16 hectares of former marshland. It began as "The SM Center North EDSA," was renamed "SM City North EDSA" the following year, and since 2022 has dropped "City" and goes by "SM North EDSA." Locals often just say "SM North," so using that shorthand with taxi drivers or local friends makes things easier.

The mall is not one building but a collection of buildings added over time. The oldest main building, City Center, was joined by The Block in 2006, the Annex building in late 2008, and the Sky Garden in May 2009. The Interior Zone and the Northlink followed, and the North Towers retail area opened in late 2018. Wikipedia says the total floor area has grown to around
and lists about 970 stores, roughly 300 of them restaurants. The numbers change as redevelopment continues, so treat them as rough figures.

For travelers, the appeal of SM North EDSA is that everything is handled in one place. Currency exchange, SIM cards from telecom companies, pharmacies and supermarkets, clothing and electronics, bookstores and toy shops, cinemas and food courts are all here, mostly in air-conditioned interiors. On a hot, humid or rainy day, few places in Manila are as easy for spending the day. The Sky Garden on the roof is especially good for anyone tired of air conditioning who wants to rest in fresh air.

Still, it helps to know that this mall is an everyday shopping destination rather than a downtown tourist sight. If you expect historic attractions like Intramuros or Rizal Park, you may be disappointed. But if you want to see how the local middle class spends a weekend, the glittering decorations of the Christmas season, or everyday life of the kind you would see visiting a Filipino household, it is actually interesting. It is especially recommended for Korean students and families staying in Quezon City, and for travelers whose plans are stuck on a rainy day.

A rooftop garden that opened in May 2009. A long, curving promenade is lined with plants and benches, and inside is the Sky Dome, an event venue of about 1,500 seats. The cool evening hours, good for walking, are the most popular.

This area first opened in July 2006, and its large oval central plaza often hosts product launches and performances. It has a large supermarket, a food hall and a chapel, and a Disney Store opened here in September 2025.

The main building area that opened in 1985. The SM department store, supermarket, food court and cinemas are grouped here, giving it the most classic mall atmosphere. An IMAX with Laser theater reopened in late 2024 (reportedly in October).

About 300 restaurants are said to be here, from Filipino home cooking to Korean, Japanese, fast food and dessert shops. Lines get long at lunchtime, so going before 11:00 or after 2 PM is much more relaxed.
You can walk from MRT-3 North Avenue station, and there is also a bus terminal inside the mall. On March 13, 2025, the SM North EDSA Busway station on the EDSA Carousel route opened.

The seventh level of the Annex 1 building is said to hold a 1.5 MW solar power installation. It is eye-catching that a mall produces its own energy, but ordinary visitors cannot go up to see it, so there is no need to look for it.
The North Towers has a retail area along with a Park Inn by Radisson hotel. It is convenient for people who have business in Quezon City and want to handle lodging and meals inside the mall.

The Philippines is a country where the Christmas mood starts in September, and the big malls compete with their decorations. From late October to early January you can see lights, trees and event stages.

items.title: Half-day course
items.subtitle: Afternoon shopping and the Sky Garden in the evening

children.text: Arrive at MRT-3 North Avenue station and enter the mall through the connecting walkway. First have a late lunch at the food court or a restaurant.
Look around the SM department store and supermarket in City Center. For gifts such as Philippine snacks, dried mango and coffee, the supermarket usually has the best prices.
Cross over to The Block to watch events in the central plaza and rest at a café. On days without events, it is mostly store browsing.
Go up to the Sky Garden at dusk for a walk. The breeze is cooler than in the daytime, and the time when the city lights come on is lovely.
Have dinner, then see a movie or finish with a massage shop. For the trip home, it is better to avoid the rush hour when MRT is crowded.
If you will be returning late, check the last train time and bus service in advance, and at night it is safer to use an app taxi such as Grab.

items.title: Full-day course
items.subtitle: The whole mall and one more Quezon City stop

children.text: Arrive when the mall opens and start leisurely with City Center. There are fewer people in the morning, so browsing is easier.
Have lunch at The Block food hall or the City Center food court. You can choose from many stalls, so it works even when your group has different tastes.
Keep walking through the Annex, the Interior Zone and the Northlink. Electronics, household goods and furniture stores are mixed together, so there is a lot to see.
Take a taxi or Grab to Quezon Memorial Circle, or stay in the mall and watch a movie.
See the sunset and evening scenery from the Sky Garden and finish the day with dinner.
From any MRT-3 station along EDSA, such as Ayala in Makati or Shaw Boulevard and Cubao around Ortigas, you can reach the northern terminus,
North Avenue station
, in one ride.
The regular fare for the full run from North Avenue to Taft Avenue is known to be
. Students, seniors and persons with disabilities get a 50% discount.
The trains are very crowded at rush hours, so wear your bag in front and keep your belongings safe.
Fares and operating hours can change, so check official MRT-3 announcements.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) to SM North EDSA it is around
20 km
by car, and it often takes more than an hour depending on traffic.
Take an airport taxi or Grab and set "SM North EDSA" as the destination. If you have a lot of luggage, a taxi is better than the train.
It is best to avoid the weekday rush hour between 4 PM and 8 PM.
The SM North EDSA Busway station on the EDSA Carousel bus route is said to have opened on March 13, 2025.
The terminal inside the mall connects with several city bus routes. Routes and fares change often, so check on site.
The buildings in the mall are linked by indoor walkways and pedestrian overpasses, and many stretches can be crossed in the rain without an umbrella.
To leave the mall, use an app taxi such as Grab or a regular taxi. Regular taxis are supposed to use the meter, so check the starting fare and that the meter is running.

SM North EDSA is an indoor mall, so you can go all year and the weather hardly affects your plans. In the rainy season, however, traffic around EDSA gets extremely congested and roads sometimes flood, so getting there becomes the bigger problem.

to
. Hours change on holidays and at year-end, so check the SM Supermalls official website first.

Eating inside the mall is really easy. City Center and The Block have food courts and a food hall, with everything from Filipino restaurants to Korean, Japanese, Chinese and fast food. Popular chains such as Jollibee and McDonald's are the easiest on the wallet, and if you miss Korean food, look for the Korean stores. The mix of shops changes often, so refer to the mall directories or the store list on the official SM website.

For lodging, the Park Inn by Radisson hotel in the mall's North Towers is the closest. Around Quezon City there are many mid-range and budget hotels and Korean-run boarding houses, which also makes it popular with people staying for a month. Prices change a lot by season, so check directly on booking sites.
When you get off at MRT-3 North Avenue station, follow the walkway that connects to the mall. At first the building divisions are confusing, so taking a photo of an entrance map helps.
The mall is very large. Don't try to see all of it at once; pick two or three target areas, such as City Center, The Block and the Sky Garden.
Because each building has its own name, when arranging a meeting be specific, such as "SM North EDSA, The Block, entrance number such-and-such."
The air conditioning is very strong. Bring a thin jacket.
Weekends and paydays (around the 15th and 30th) are crowded. For a quiet visit, weekday mornings are best.
Use the taxi stands outside the mall, and decide where to meet your Grab car in advance when it is crowded.
You can use the exchange counters inside the mall, but rates differ between shops, so compare two or three.
Hours and events change often, so check official SM notices before you visit.
In the crowded mall and on MRT-3, pickpocketing and phone snatching can happen, so always keep your belongings in front of you.
Traffic around EDSA is very heavy on weekends, paydays and at year-end. Allow plenty of travel time.
There are bag checks at the entrances, and large bags or suitcases may be restricted or not allowed in.
Roads around the mall can flood on rainy days, so check the weather forecast.
Some taxi drivers try to bargain instead of using the meter; refuse and take another car or use an app.
It is wise to carry a copy of your passport and leave valuables at your lodging.
A city park that takes about
20–40 minutes
by taxi or Grab depending on traffic. Many local families walk and jog there, so it pairs well with the mall as a full-day plan.
A nature park in the city, in the north of Quezon City. It is some distance away, so going by car is best, and travel time varies greatly with traffic.
A mixed-use district east of Quezon City with cafés and restaurants clustered together, good for an evening stop. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so check on Grab.
